searchText: I believe your pre-coffee comment was correct. You can't drive PoW down to 1s block times indefinitely. Any thoughts on the recent comments from Justin Sun about the merge? https://www.coindesk.com/business/2022/08/05/justin-sun-backs-ethereum-hard-fork-as-merge-approaches/ Someone please tell me we are not going to have 3 Ethereums post merge? This isn't really the right server to discuss the thoughts and actions of pop culture personalities. thats a very generous description of Justin Yeah maybe should have worded better. Is this possible or what can be done to prevent it Anyone can fork Ethereum at any time. This is by design. Users are free to use any version of Ethereum they want as well. It is impossible to prevent this (by design). Does EIP-1559 change the way tiebreakers happen when you determine which block to uncle? Since now the basefee decreasing/increasing determines a large portion of the bribe due to legacy transactions and more transactions being eligible with lower basefee..... wouldn't it make sense to pick the block with the lowest gas utilization, instead of the first block observed, or the block with the highest total difficulty to break a tie? why 3, we need classic + eth1.0ProgPOW + eth1.0 + eth2.0 at least > will make the network much cheaper, **faster** and environmentally friendly. Seems like people still believe that the merge will speed up something It does, marginally What do you mean? Slot times decrease to 12 seconds, so slightly faster. The cool, inherent security feature in PoS you would need 67% of the staking validators. This means a significant long investment into an asset you would need to attack. Very unlikely one would do that and risk that investment. In PoW you could rent much hashrate for a few minutes to attack the chain. Energy consumption issues aside, I'd still go for 100% PoS. The ideal attack would be an eth loan, short eth, crash price, repay loan. But thats assuming you could borrow enough eth which isn't currently doable. Maybe if validation becomes unattractive and enough withdraw it'll become a worry. You can rent usage of people's staked eth too Will be interesting and scary when people provide that service. I assume eth devs will need to fork to prevent it if it becomes popular. the biggest problem I have with POS is that currently there is a small number of pool operators that put an incredible amount of effort into running their nodes as efficiently and reliably as possible The people that run pools are those that are good at running pools, and probably barely mine themselves for the most part. With POS, we have people that want to invest and collect a percentage that all of a sudden need to run the nodes that keep the network running smoothly. These are 2 completely separate skillsets, and I think it will result in non-stop pain. Either we will have the hashpower/stakepower centralized among a few people that know what they are doing, or we will have non-stop madness. For example I predict that 90% of validator nodes are going to move into AWS US-East so they have good latency with each other and the coin will be even more centralized then before when you at least had to be geographically close to a miner to maintain it A big part of the EL nodes are already on hosting services https://ethernodes.org/network-types how would you prevent that? can we rename it AWS coin when it reaches 67%? incentives for being spread out geographically, incentives to make your own blocks/requirements to do so, extreme randomization of rewards to prevent profitable nicehash (or whatever such a service is called), and honestly I'm sure people could come up with smarter solutions than me. Sounds like a lot of complexity for almost no gain 😅 TBH the existing PoS is better compared to that Also you aware that the max you can rent is ~25 TH/s? It’s 3.3% of the network hashrate, which is 900 TH/s. (Source: NH and MRR) Plus even if you magically manage to obtain 51% of hashrate, you’d need a lot of time to ensure that the attack is successful, as the block production on PoW is poisson-distributed. more like 50-60th you get more hashrate the more you pay, as more miners change algo True, let it be 50-60 TH/s. Still changes nothing though can I rent your hashpower? Right before ZIL starts, it is worth a lot and is not even mining ZIL :D Also, don't forget that we are still have to see how less reliable PoS is compared to PoW. Don't expect something that makes Ethereum three times as complex being as reliable as ~1k lines of code, which PoW is. also a 51% attack reduces the value of all the miners that participated in it, as the news about it will tank the value of the coin so there is an incentive for miners to avoid selling their hashpower to one also the NFT craze is proof that people can't 51% ethereum as there is about $1-2m on a regular basis available if you 51% mined all the blocks for yourself for 2-5 minutes > Energy consumption issues aside, I'd still go for 100% PoS. So I'm not sure why you say that PoS is a go-to in 100%. Unfortunately PoS is not a drop-in replacement. Yes PoW consumes electricity, yes PoW produces CO2, but the level of reliability and code-efficiency it provides cannot compare to anything. AWS already has 51% of POS how do you incentivize that? so when MEV starts moving to POS, everyone that likes money will move to AWS to have the lowest latency you can't incentivize high latency Helium managed the geographically distant part not without making it more centralized Helium is a bunch of fake APs with air simualtors inbetween them or it was :D Through fully trusted hardware That you have to buy from approved vendors so it became a centralized coin, just like Ethereum is Let's see how PoS works out on mainnet. It seems to be fine on testnet. have you offered 10k eth prizes to anyone that can do a mildly inconvenient thign on testnet? people will not put in the effort until it is on main net and settled, then they will break stuff in fun ways to profit or just be an ass the average home miner is not competitive and makes money off increases in coin value more than the difference between power and hash values It is a hobby for us because we would make far more money at a day job for the time and effort invested and how many hours of education and time is ivested to do that? good way to burn down the place with a sata to pcie adapter before power costs with a $2000 card there were a few days when eth shot up that the current hashrate made a lot. Then more hashrate came onboard and it evened out again. The nature of things. People who bought eth and staked at $200 did very well for a while too. Has it? 0.0 I thought a little more than double Wow never noticed

With POS, we have people that want to invest and collect a percentage that all of a sudden need to run the nodes that keep the network running smoothly. These are 2 completely separate skillsets, and I think it will result in non-stop pain.
